data.rule:
16 Nov 2026: what the post-average renormalization of the soma/neurite fractions changes in the MRI template.
mri/code/ship_template.py (the build of record, template/mri/provenance.json; profile "rebuild"): each input's warped fractions are
renormalized per input (f / (f1 + f2) inside its micro mask & model mask), then averaged over the inputs whose warped model mask >= 0.5
(plain mean), clipped to [0, 1], renormalized again (f / (f1 + f2) where the sum > 0), symmetrized (A + M(A)) / 2 and cut to the union
of the model masks. This script recomputes the average from template/mri/_work (the build's own per-input files; sizes match the
provenance's 40 _work inputs), checks that renormalize + symmetrize + cut reproduces linc_mri_frac1/2, and measures, BEFORE the
renormalization, |f1 + f2 - 1| in the template brain mask, by where it occurs:
  covered_interior : all 8 inputs' model and micro masks cover the voxel, and it is > 1 mm inside the brain outline
  partial_coverage : at least one input's model or micro mask does not cover it (and > 1 mm inside the outline)
  border           : within 1 mm of the brain outline
and the change of each fraction (|f_after - f_before|). Read-only; writes paper/numbers/mri_template_frac_renormalization.json.
    (run by the analysis's saved script in the MRI registration environment)

shipped_after_symmetrization.cause: the symmetrization (A + M(A)) / 2 runs AFTER the renormalization: where a voxel's mirror had no fraction data (sum 0 before the renormalization), the shipped sum is 0.5 x (1 + 0) or similar

cause_before.explanation: each input's fractions are 0 where its micro mask does not cover the voxel but its model mask does; averaging over the model masks then lowers the sum below 1 there (not exactly k/8: the masks and fractions are interpolated at their edges)

data.note: frac2 = 1 - frac1 wherever the sum is > 0 after the renormalization, so the two shipped fractions carry one degree of freedom; the per-input renormalization (before averaging) is the same rule applied to each input
